dedupe_keys.name: data and code for administered gas pricing no longer constrains refinery heat integration in the gulf evidence from a nine case portfolio

description: This Zenodo release supplies Python code and a nine-case crude-distillation retrofit portfolio for evaluating break-even industrial gas tariffs. A public README lists a JSON case table, tariff solver, figure script and dependency on a separate crude-distillation heat-integration code deposit. The authors compare portfolio economics with Oman gas tariffs over 2012–2026; the model can test investment sensitivity to fuel price, capital cost and case assumptions in refinery-energy scenarios. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this solver and portfolio. The first review rejected the linked infrastructure study as unrelated single-study data, but reusable code and an explicit dependency are public. A limitation is that case values mix reported, derived and adopted assumptions, so results are conditional, not measured refinery savings. The dependency lists a file with a suffix where this README names an unsuffixed filename; execution may require adjustment. Zenodo states CC BY 4.0 and free public files. Neither Python file was run, and no tariff threshold was reproduced.
